{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash
#FLUX: -N 1
#FLUX: -n 1
#FLUX: -c 1
#FLUX: -t 4h
#FLUX: -o /nobackup/gamatull/stdout
#FLUX: -e /nobackup/gamatull/stderr

# The PBS -q directive is not directly translatable to Flux.
# Flux does not have traditional queues; resource allocation is managed by the scheduler based on priority and available resources.

# The PBS -V directive, which exports all environment variables, is not directly translated.
# Flux has a different model for environment management. By default, Flux does not propagate the user's environment.
# To pass specific variables, use the --environment option (e.g., #FLUX: --environment=VAR1,VAR2).

echo /u/gamatull/scripts/LST/sc3_pixelcount_MOYD11A2.sh

export  SENS=$SENS

export INSENS=/nobackupp8/gamatull/dataproces/LST/${SENS}11A2_mean_msk
export OUTSENS=/nobackupp8/gamatull/dataproces/LST/${SENS}11A2_mean_msk/txt

export RAMDIR=/dev/shm


cat /nobackup/gamatull/dataproces/LST/geo_file/list_day.txt   | xargs -n 1 -P 46  bash -c $' 
day=$1

gdal_edit.py  -a_nodata -1   $INSENS/${SENS}_CLOUD3k_day${day}_wgs84.tif
pkinfo -hist -i  $INSENS/${SENS}_CLOUD3k_day${day}_wgs84.tif |  awk -v day=$day \'{ if (NR==1) {   printf ("%i " , day ) ; printf ("%i " , $2) } else {   printf ("%i\\n" , $2) }  }\'

' _   | sort -k 1,1 -g  >  $OUTSENS/count_CLOUD3k.txt"
}
